summary: Scan personal data on regex-declaration lines
body: When a scanned line starts with a pattern such as `const EMAIL = /.../` and contains personal data later on that line, `PATTERN_CODE` sets `codePattern` and this branch skips `scanPersonal` for the entire line; for example, `const EMAIL = /.+/; // alice@company.co` produces no finding. This lets personal data pass the privacy gate; restrict the exemption to the regex text instead of suppressing the whole line.

summary: Clear disabled rules before card validation
body: `run()` merges this environment with `process.env`, so if the postmaster process has `SCRUB_CHECK_DISABLE=email`, the description scan skips email detection and can accept a card containing an unlogged email. Clear `SCRUB_CHECK_DISABLE` for this security-sensitive scan.

If `raw/archive` is a symlink to a directory outside the checkout, a destination such as `raw/archive/record` passes the lexical path check; this recursive `mkdir` and the later rename follow the symlink and write the promoted copy outside the project. Reject symlinked destination ancestors or verify the physical destination stays within the repository.

summary: Verify bundle contents, not only the source hash
body: In `--check` mode, a matching hash in the bundle header causes an early return without checking the generated body. Editing or corrupting `scrub-check.ts` or `raw-promote.ts` while retaining that header therefore passes the check even though the wrappers execute divergent code; compare the bundle with a fresh build or verify a digest of its contents.
